diagnostic_evidence.quote: Denote by $\Ss_n^X$ the family of all linear sampling algorithms $S_k^X$ in $L_2(U,X;\mu)$ of the form \eqref{S_k} with $k \le n$.

issues.failure_explanation: $S_{c_3n}^X$ uses $c_3n>n$ sample points, so it is not admissible in the infimum over $\Ss_n^X$ defining $\varrho_n$; the error of an algorithm with more samples can be arbitrarily smaller than $\varrho_n$, so the first '$\ll$' is false. Counterexample within the hypotheses: $\sigma_s=2^s$ (so $d_s=2^{-s-1}$), any $0<q<2$; then $\varrho_n(B^q)\ge d_n\ge cM2^{-n}$, while with high probability $\sup_{v\in B^q}\|v-S_{c_3n}^Xv\|\le M\sqrt{n^{-1}\sum_{s\ge n}d_s^2}\le CM2^{-n}/\sqrt{n}$, so the ratio grows like $\sqrt{n}$. Only $\varrho_{c_3n}\le\sup_v\|v-S_{c_3n}^Xv\|$ is trivially true.

issues.why_classification: The false intermediate inequality is repaired by a routine local reindexing; all stated rates and guarantees survive.

issues.failure_explanation: For a single-index multi-index $\bs=se_j$ the displayed weight is $\sigma_\bs^2=\sum_{s'\le\min(s,\eta)}\binom{s}{s'}\rho_j^{2s'}\asymp s^\eta\rho_j^{2\eta}$, so $\sum_{\bs\in\FF}\sigma_\bs^{-q}\ge\sum_s c\,s^{-\eta q/2}$, which diverges whenever $\eta q\le2$ (e.g. $\eta=1$ for any $q<2$, or $\eta=2$ for $q\le1$), independently of $(\rho_j)$. Hence the asserted $\|\bsigma^{-1}\|_{\ell_q}\le N<\infty$ is false for such $\eta$, contradicting 'for any $\eta\in\NN$'; it holds only under the additional constraint $\eta>2/q$ (then $\sum_{\bs}\sigma_\bs^{-q}\le C\prod_j(1+C\rho_j^{-q})<\infty$ using $(\rho_j^{-1})\in\ell_q$).

issues.failure_explanation: With $q=p/(1-p)$ and the weight \eqref{sigma_s}, the same computation as for the lognormal lemma gives $\sum_{\bs\in\FF}\sigma_\bs^{-q}=\infty$ whenever $\eta q\le2$, i.e. $\eta\le2(1-p)/p$ (e.g. $p=1/2$ with $\eta\in\{1,2\}$), since for $\bs=se_j$ the weight grows only like $s^{\eta/2}$; the lemma claims the $\ell_q$-bound for arbitrary $\eta\in\NN$. Moreover, in the dependent Theorem theorem:sampling-lognormal-holomorphic the parameter $\eta$ is never quantified (it appears free in the hypothesis), and the hypothesis couples $\eta$ into the condition $b_j^{p-1}\frac{\xi}{4\sqrt{\eta!}}\|\bb\|_{\ell_p}>1$, which becomes harder as $\eta$ grows; after repairing the lemma (requiring $\eta>2(1-p)/p$), the theorem's stated hypotheses no longer guarantee an admissible $\eta$.
